source: Owner task issue #317 (created 2026-10-06T04:02:54Z by the owner's account) and tasks/ACTIVE-TASK.json task uda-universal-enforcement-coverage-20261006. The owner handed the task to this Claude session on 2026-10-06 ('continue, sent some work in your lane').
problem: UDA rules can exist as prose, an index entry, a rule-graph node or a sentence test without any path to the task-time boundary where they would change or block the answer. On 2026-10-06, 70 patterns were indexed but structured task-time metadata sourced only 5 of them. A wildcard 'patterns/*' legacy entry implied coverage. Semantic obligations always ended UNKNOWN, with no way to bind evidence. A simple operational request then received a dominated two-command route next to the better one-command route, although existing guidance already said to use the smallest sufficient method and to minimize owner choice.
owner_corrections: Repair UDA so applicable rules are not merely stored as prose or indexed, but reliably reach the task-time boundary where they can change or block the actual answer/action.
Do **not** make this a one-off fix for a PDF-command mistake. The owner’s concern is systemic: there are likely many UDA rules that exist but are not actually enforced.

Success is not “add another rule saying to follow rules.” Success requires an inspectable path from rule → applicability/trigger → obligation → correct boundary → evidence/check → admission, plus regressions that fail if that path silently breaks.
continue, sent some work in your lane
failure_mechanisms: Coverage: an active rule can be index-routed prose with no explicit enforcement disposition.
Trigger: a discoverable rule can lack an explicit task-time activation route; 31 of 70 index entries had no leading trigger, and 16 pattern files were not indexed at all.
Admission: semantic obligations had no way to bind PASS or FAIL evidence to the exact candidate, so they could only block or be ignored.
Bootstrap: a turn that never loaded UDA cannot be protected by UDA, but nothing stated that.
Regression: tests proved that rule text exists, not that violating work is blocked.
existing_coverage: patterns/reasoning-selection.md (smallest sufficient method, minimum owner choice)
required_behavior: Every active indexed UDA rule and pattern has exactly one explicit enforcement disposition.
A wildcard, an index listing, a rule-graph node or a sentence test never counts as enforcement proof.
A new unclassified rule, or one that adds legacy-unstructured backlog without the owner's authorization, fails the audit.

Semantic obligations can receive PASS, FAIL or NOT_APPLICABLE evidence bound to the exact contract, obligation, phase, destination and payload. Mechanical code verifies the binding and never claims to prove the judgment.
The dominated-route regression rejects the old answer and admits the repaired one.
UDA distinguishes an activated, enforced task from one that is NOT_ACTIVATED or OUTSIDE_UDA.
The external simple-turn bootstrap exemption is reported truthfully, with the exact owner-side instruction change.

nonclaims: A matching receipt verifies the binding and attributes an asserted judgment to an actor; it does not prove application, semantic truth, actor identity or actual independence. SAME_AGENT is application evidence, not independent verification.
